note: Scheduled US events whose DATES come from FRED's release calendar (api.stlouisfed.org/fred/release/dates; FRED API terms OPEN, same key as futures_state). Add a release as a row here, never in code. `name_contains` is checked against the name FRED returns for the id before any date is used: an id that answers with another name writes nothing. `at`/`tz` is the publisher's own fixed wall-clock release time, a convention applied to every row (time_basis says so); `from` is the first date that convention holds. Releases whose history already comes from first prints in futures_state (payrolls, CPI, claims, retail sales, PCE, industrial production, JOLTS) are NOT repeated here, so the event index does not see one release twice. `per_year` is the [low, high] count of past dates a typical complete year must hold; outside it the release writes nothing (FRED lists load dates, and a release that is really daily series would list every business day). `usual_weekdays` (Mon=0) only counts past dates off the usual day in the report, e.g. unscheduled FOMC actions, which still carry the convention stamp. `window_h` (+/- hours) is carried on every row because the times of day here are unverified conventions.

releases.title: FOMC Statement
releases.why: the policy decision: the largest scheduled repricing of USD rates and gold. 14:00 ET since March 2013; earlier statements came at other times and are left out rather than mis-stamped. Unscheduled inter-meeting actions appear on their own dates and carry the same stamp, which may be wrong for them
